beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — open on the Claude UI, ask shown answered
beats.narration_text: Annyeonghaseyo, Liam. One Claude prompt. A maturation staircase, a VERM bar across the middle, and what happens when therapy removes it — differentiation block, animated.

props.command: claude "Port the differentiation-block plate into a Manim scene — two-panel staircase: left blocked (VERM bar, SKY pile-up), right released (GREEN flow arrow, BLUE star at top)."

beats.role_note: The mechanism before the build — AML differentiation stall and ATRA release
beats.narration_text: Normal blood cells mature through a series of stages — an ascending staircase from stem cell to specialized function. AML freezes that process. Cells are stuck at an early rung, pile up, and can't mature. This plate shows that stall and what it looks like when differentiation therapy releases it.
beats.visual_intent: Slate — two staircase panels labeled BLOCKED and RELEASED; step labels: stem → progenitor → precursor → mature; AML block arrow at step 1-2

beats.role_note: Stakes before the build — ATRA in AML as differentiation therapy proof of concept
beats.narration_text: ATRA in AML is the classic case. It doesn't kill the cells — it releases the block. The cells that were piling up below the bar resume climbing the staircase and mature into functional granulocytes. The plate's two panels are the before and after.
beats.visual_intent: Slate — stat card: ATRA + arsenic trioxide achieves >90% CR in APL; 'release not kill' annotation; before/after staircase thumbnails

beats.role_note: ClaudeComposerAsk — the REAL Claude Code prompt. SPARK-LINE LAW: greeting = 'The ask,'
beats.narration_text: The ask. Into Claude: port the differentiation-block plate from plates underscore gen dot py p-zero-nine into Manim. Two-panel staircase side by side. Left panel: five ascending step-nodes connected by GRAY arrows, a VERM bar cutting across between step one and step two, and eight small SKY circles piled up below the bar. Right panel: same five step-nodes connected by GREEN arrows, a BLUE star at the top step. Animate left panel first — build the steps, place the bar, accumulate the pile — then right panel with GREEN flow arrow and the star at top.

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the ACTUAL B05_DifferentiationBlock class, trimmed to what teaches
beats.narration_text: Read it. The staircase is computed by a helper function that generates the five step positions as a diagonal progression — each step shifts right and up by a fixed delta. The step nodes are circles, not rectangles, because the p09 plate uses circles for immature cell state and a star polygon for the mature end-point. The VERM bar is a Rectangle rotated forty-five degrees to cut across the diagonal between step one and step two. The pile-up is a LaggedStart FadeIn of eight small SKY circles placed below the bar. The right panel is the same staircase with GREEN arrows drawn as a single flow line from base to star, not individual step-to-step arrows.

props.title: scenes.py — B05_DifferentiationBlock
props.code:
# scenes.py — Claude Code output
config.background_color = "#FFFFFF"
SKY="#56B4E9"; BLUE="#0072B2"; GREEN="#009E73"
VERM="#D55E00"; GRAY="#7c7c7c"

STEPS=5; DX=1.15; DY=0.72

def step_pts(x0,y0):
  return [(x0+i*DX, y0-i*DY) for i in range(STEPS)]

class B05_DifferentiationBlock(Scene):
  def construct(self):
    # LEFT PANEL — blocked
    pts_L = step_pts(-5.2, 1.2)
    nodes_L = VGroup(*[Circle(0.26,color=SKY,
      fill_color=SKY,fill_opacity=0.38,stroke_width=2.4
      ).move_to([x,y,0]) for x,y in pts_L])
    arrows_L = VGroup(*[Arrow([pts_L[i][0],pts_L[i][1],0],
      [pts_L[i+1][0],pts_L[i+1][1],0],buff=0.28,
      color=GRAY,stroke_width=2.2,
      max_tip_length_to_length_ratio=0.22)
      for i in range(STEPS-1)])
    # VERM bar — diagonal cut
    bx=(pts_L[1][0]+pts_L[2][0])/2
    by=(pts_L[1][1]+pts_L[2][1])/2
    bar=Rectangle(width=0.22,height=1.1,fill_color=VERM,
      fill_opacity=0.8,stroke_color=VERM,stroke_width=3
      ).rotate(-PI/4).move_to([bx,by,0])
    # Pile-up circles
    pile=[Circle(0.18,color=SKY,fill_color=SKY,
      fill_opacity=0.52,stroke_width=1.6).move_to(
      [pts_L[1][0]+dx,pts_L[1][1]+dy,0])
      for dx,dy in [(-0.35,0.55),(0.05,0.6),(0.42,0.52),
                    (-0.12,0.95),(0.28,0.9),(0.62,0.78),
                    (-0.4,1.28),(0.1,1.32)]]
    # Star at top of left panel (dim)
    star_L = Star(n=6,outer_radius=0.36,inner_radius=0.16,
      color=BLUE,fill_color=BLUE,fill_opacity=0.18,
      stroke_width=2.2).move_to([pts_L[-1][0],pts_L[-1][1],0])
    # RIGHT PANEL — released
    pts_R = step_pts(0.6, 1.2)
    nodes_R = VGroup(*[Circle(0.26,color=SKY,
      fill_color=SKY,fill_opacity=0.38,stroke_width=2.4
      ).move_to([x,y,0]) for x,y in pts_R])
    flow = Arrow([pts_R[0][0],pts_R[0][1],0],
      [pts_R[-1][0],pts_R[-1][1],0],buff=0.28,
      color=GREEN,stroke_width=3.8,
      max_tip_length_to_length_ratio=0.14)
    star_R = Star(n=6,outer_radius=0.36,inner_radius=0.16,
      color=BLUE,fill_color=BLUE,fill_opacity=0.55,
      stroke_width=2.4).move_to([pts_R[-1][0],pts_R[-1][1],0])
    # Animate left
    self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(n) for n in nodes_L],
      lag_ratio=0.2,run_time=0.9))
    self.play(LaggedStart(*[GrowArrow(a) for a in arrows_L],
      lag_ratio=0.18,run_time=0.8))
    self.play(FadeIn(bar),run_time=0.3)
    self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(p) for p in pile],
      lag_ratio=0.14,run_time=0.9))
    self.play(FadeIn(star_L),run_time=0.3)
    self.wait(0.4)
    # Animate right
    self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(n) for n in nodes_R],
      lag_ratio=0.2,run_time=0.8))
    self.play(GrowArrow(flow),run_time=0.5)
    self.play(FadeIn(star_R),run_time=0.35)
    self.wait(0.7)

beats.role_note: Manim render of B05_DifferentiationBlock — blocked left panel, released right panel
beats.narration_text: Run it. Left panel: the five step-nodes appear bottom to top, GRAY arrows connect them, the VERM bar drops across the diagonal between steps one and two, and the SKY circles accumulate below it. The star at the top is dim — unreachable. Then the right panel: same five steps, a single GREEN arrow sweeps from base to top, and the BLUE star appears at full brightness. Two panels, two states, side by side.

beats.role_note: ClaudeComposerAsk — revision prompt. SPARK-LINE LAW: greeting = 'The change,'
beats.narration_text: The change. Revise: after building the blocked state, animate the release. The VERM bar fades out. The piled circles start moving up the staircase with LaggedStart — they climb toward the top. A GREEN arrow grows upward through the cleared path. The BLUE star brightens by animating its fill opacity from eighteen percent to full. Show the therapy as motion: the pile resolving into the flow upward makes the treatment tangible.

props.command:
claude "Revise: after building the blocked state, animate the release.
VERM bar FadeOut, piled circles move up the staircase (LaggedStart),
GREEN arrow grows upward, BLUE star brightens. Show the therapy as motion."

beats.role_note: Manim render of B07_DifferentiationBlockRelease — blocked → animated release
beats.narration_text: Watch the revision. The blocked state builds: steps, bar, pile. Then the bar fades out. Watch the pile: the circles start moving up the staircase one by one with LaggedStart — the cells that were stuck resume their climb. The GREEN arrow grows upward through the path that is now clear. The star brightens. The therapy is not subtraction — it is restoration of a process that was already there, waiting.

beats.role_note: What we built and what the motion taught
beats.narration_text: Release, not kill. The animation made the therapeutic action concrete: the pile was there because of the bar, not because the cells couldn't mature. Remove the bar, the pile resolves.
beats.visual_intent: Slate — summary card: differentiation therapy logic: block removal not cytotoxicity; pile resolves to flow; 'strip this pattern for any maturation staircase'

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — suggested prompt typed in, read aloud AND discussed. greeting = 'Your turn.'
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take this prompt into Claude: add a third state to the right of the released panel — an over-differentiation state. Show the same staircase but with all nodes arriving at the top step as a crowded cluster, and a VERM X-mark on the star to show the cells have differentiated past the point of function. Why run it? Because differentiation therapy has a failure mode: over-differentiation syndrome, where the release is too fast or too complete. Showing a third state — stuck, released, over-differentiated — makes the therapeutic window visual. The student can then see why dose titration matters: you want the flow arrow, not the pile, but you also don't want all the cells arriving at the star simultaneously.

circles arrive at the top node as a crowded cluster, with a VERM X-mark on
the BLUE star. Show: blocked → released → over-differentiated."
